# Results — Study 115 (Credit-Spreads) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Tickers: HYG, LQD, IEF, SPY
(Yahoo Finance daily adjusted-close, 2010-01-04 to 2026-06-12).  Two credit-spread
ETF proxies (HYG-IEF and HYG/LQD) are used because FRED OAS data is unavailable in
this environment — we say so here and in the notebooks.  The regime flag
(stress vs calm) is set by a rolling 20-day spread proxy vs its trailing 60-day
rolling median.  Forward equity return: SPY over the next N days.  As-of **2026-06-13**.*

## The honest test — 5-day forward SPY return, by credit-regime

N = 4,111 days (after 20-day spread + 60-day rolling-median formation lag and dropping
the last 5 days with no forward return).

### Proxy 1: HYG-IEF rolling 20-day return (negative = HY underperforms Treasuries)

| Regime | n | mean fwd SPY (bps) | win-rate | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Stress** (spread < median) | 2,152 | **+25.2** | 59.7% | +2.64 |
| **Calm** (spread ≥ median) | 1,959 | **+34.1** | 63.3% | +4.26 |
| Unconditional | 4,111 | +29.4 | 61.4% | — |
| **Stress − Calm (key number)** | — | **−8.9** | — | **−0.71** |

- **Correlation** (20-day HYG-IEF spread → 5-day forward SPY): **−0.063**
- The direction of the stress−calm difference is correct (stress has lower forward returns),
  but the HAC t-stat of **−0.71** is far below the −2 bar.  The effect is economically
  small and statistically invisible.

### Proxy 2: HYG/LQD rolling 20-day relative strength (negative = HY underperforms IG)

| Regime | n | mean fwd SPY (bps) | win-rate | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Stress** (RS < median) | 2,105 | **+32.1** | 61.9% | +3.44 |
| **Calm** (RS ≥ median) | 2,006 | **+26.7** | 61.0% | +3.33 |
| Unconditional | 4,111 | +29.4 | 61.4% | — |
| **Stress − Calm (key number)** | — | **+5.4** | — | **+0.44** |

- **Correlation** (20-day HYG/LQD RS → 5-day forward SPY): **−0.062**
- The HYG/LQD proxy produces the **wrong sign**: stress periods actually have *higher*
  5-day forward SPY returns in this sample (+32.1 vs +26.7 bps).  The t-stat is +0.44
  — noise.

## 21-day forward SPY return

| Proxy | Stress (bps) | Calm (bps) | Diff (bps) | HAC t | Corr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| HYG-IEF | +113.8 | +133.6 | **−19.8** | **−0.60** | −0.122 |
| HYG/LQD | +127.8 | +118.5 | **+9.3** | **+0.28** | −0.072 |

At the 21-day horizon, the correlation (−0.122) hints at an economic direction but the
t-stat remains well below the inference bar.  The signal is predominantly coincident
with, not predictive of, equity stress at the ETF-proxy frequency.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The HYG-IEF direction is correct (stress → lower equity forward
  returns) but the HAC t-stat on the stress-minus-calm difference peaks at −0.71 (5d)
  / −0.60 (21d), well below the |t| ≥ 2 bar.  The HYG/LQD proxy has the wrong sign
  at 5 days (+0.44).  Correlation −0.06 to −0.12 is economically plausible but
  statistically weak.  Literature support alone earns WEAK; t-stats do not support REAL.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even if the directional signal were real, the ETF-spread
  proxy is a slow-moving 20-day return — it switches regimes infrequently and lags the
  actual credit events it tries to capture.  Daily rebalancing on a noisy binary regime
  flag at this magnitude would be eaten by costs and slippage.  **No profitable trading
  rule is demonstrated.**
- **Beats buy-and-hold? — NOT SUPPORTED.** In both stress and calm regimes, SPY has
  positive forward returns.  The credit-spread regime flag does not identify windows
  where going short or flat SPY is justified by the data.
